action_args.rationale: Testing trimmed_mean to handle unstable ranking and potential outliers in the ensemble.

trajectory.thought: The series has high trend and seasonal strength but unstable ranking (tau=0.259). The previous trimmed_mean was a robust baseline. To address the instability and potential for complementary errors, I will test a simple unweighted mean over the full pool to see if averaging reduces variance without trimming, leveraging the "robust" combination hint.

The ranking stability is very low (tau=0.259), and NaiveSeasonal wins on different windows than ARIMA or DWT_catboost, indicating strong seasonality with shifting dynamics. A simple mean may underweight the robust seasonal baseline in some contexts. I will test a weighted combination using inverse error weights to give more influence to the currently top-performing models (NaiveSeasonal, DWT_catboost) while still retaining diversity from the rest of the pool to mitigate correlation risks.

The current leader uses a weighted combination on a subset (pool4) which excluded NaiveSeasonal and NaiveMovingAverage. However, NaiveSeasonal is the overall top performer in the error table and has strong seasonal correlation. Excluding it might have hurt robustness given the "unstable" ranking verdict. I will test a simple median combination over the full pool to see if including the best individual model (NaiveSeasonal) via a robust aggregator improves performance, serving as a baseline against the weighted subset approach.

To test robustness against this instability and potentially reduce variance from the weight estimation, I will try a DBA (Dynamic Basis Alignment) combination on the full pool. DBA often finds better consensus among correlated models by aligning their basis functions, which could be more stable than inverse-error weighting for this high-trend, low-stability series.
